home.about: I'm **Kartikeyan C**, a product & UI/UX designer with **14+ years** of experience *who blends clear thinking with visual craft* — from interfaces and brand identities to motion. I work full-time and take on freelance projects, and I measure my work by what it helps people achieve.

about.lead: A product & UI/UX designer from Chennai who turns complex ideas into simple, useful experiences.

intros.label: For anyone
intros.text: I'm **Kartikeyan** — a Chennai-based product & UI/UX designer who blends clear thinking with visual craft, from interfaces and brand identities to motion.

intros.label: Recruiters
intros.text: I'm a **product & UI/UX designer with 14+ years of experience**, taking work from research and flows to polished UI — plus logo and motion design. I work full-time and take on freelance projects; based in Chennai and happy to talk about roles, on-site or remote.

intros.label: Product teams
intros.text: I design in **flows, components and prototypes**, so work is easy to test, build and scale. Expect clear handoff, reusable patterns and a design-system mindset.

intros.label: Founders & clients
intros.text: Need a product, a brand, or both? I can design **the website or app and the identity around it** — like the Milton store and the Nexura logo — so everything feels like one brand.

story: I work across **product design, UI/UX, logo design and motion** — *so I think about a product end to end: how it works, how it looks and how it feels to use.*
My work ranges from e-commerce experiences like **Milton** to brand identities like **Nexura**. *Whatever the brief, I start with the people using it.*

principles.title: People first
principles.text: Every decision starts with who is using the product and what they need to do.

principles.title: Clarity
principles.text: Simple layouts, clear hierarchy and no unnecessary steps.

principles.title: Consistency
principles.text: Reusable components and brand rules that keep everything coherent.

principles.title: Purposeful motion
principles.text: Animation that explains and delights — never just decoration.

projects.lead: Product, UI/UX and brand identity work — case studies from research to shipped screens.

services.lead: Product and UI/UX design first, backed by brand and motion craft — one goal: products that are clear, consistent and a joy to use.

contact.lead: Have a product, brand or idea? Tell me a little about it and I'll get back to you.

faq.q: What kind of projects do you take on?
faq.a: Product design, UI/UX for websites and apps, graphic design (logos, posters, brochures and company decks), motion design and video editing — end to end or just one part.

faq.a: A short description of the project, who it's for, your timeline and any existing material like brand files or wireframes.

faq.q: Do you work with clients outside Chennai?
faq.a: Yes — I'm happy to work remotely.

projects.name: Nexura

caseStudy.title: Nexura: a brand identity and website for an AI integration firm
caseStudy.role: Logo, identity, UX/UI design and front-end development
caseStudy.background: **Nexura Infotech** builds AI into the systems of banks, insurers, payment firms and pharmaceutical manufacturers. I designed its logo and identity, then designed and built its **25-page website**.
caseStudy.challenge: Tech logos often end up as a generic letter in a box. The aim was a mark that could only belong to **Nexura**, built from the name itself, that still works in **one colour, at small sizes** and on everything from an ID card to an exhibition stand.
goals: A mark built from the name, not a generic symbol
Works in full colour, in a single colour and in black and white
Clear on a business card and on an exhibition stand
A simple colour and type system the team can reuse

process.title: The mark
process.text: A hexagon made of folded strips: solid and dependable, with a sense of movement in the folds. The NEXURA wordmark and the tagline sit underneath as one lock-up.

process.title: Six letters, one shape
process.text: Each fold traces a letter. N, E, X, U, R and A can all be found inside the one hexagon, so the mark literally spells the name.

process.title: Colour
process.text: Four colours, blue, green, red and orange, make up the full-colour mark. Each one also works as a solid background with the logo reversed in white.

process.title: Monochrome and pattern
process.text: A black-and-white version for single-colour printing, and a repeat pattern cut from the mark for backgrounds and merchandise.

process.title: Typography
process.text: Sora and Satoshi Variable as the brand typefaces, both clean geometric sans-serifs that sit comfortably next to the mark.

deliverables: Logo: full colour, single colour, black and white
Mockups: ID card, office glass, bottle, exhibition stand, business cards
Website: 25 pages, designed and built (HTML, CSS, JavaScript)
caseStudy.outcome: Shipped the Nexura identity — a hexagon that hides all six letters — and a 25-page website I designed and built.

projects.description: A brand identity and a 25-page website for Nexura Infotech, an AI integration firm for banks and pharma: a hexagonal mark that hides all six letters of the name, and a calm, colour-coded site I designed and built.

projects.name: RESPAY
projects.alt: RESPAY money saving app: the RESPAY logo and 'Money saving app' title beside a phone showing the transactions screen
projects.description: A money saving app for young people and families: it spots unwanted spending, and brings budgets, goals, savings, investment and insurance together in one place.

caseStudy.title: RESPAY: a money saving app for young earners
caseStudy.role: UX research and UI design: research to high-fidelity screens and prototype
caseStudy.background: **RESPAY** is a money saving app for youngsters and families. It identifies **unwanted spending** and points it out, and it's built for people who struggle with saving, investing and insurance. The goal: an interface that's easy to use every day.
caseStudy.challenge: Some young people don't save money and don't know how to start, and many spend without noticing. The users I interviewed said it plainly: *"I'm trying to save but can't"*, *"I pay 50% of my salary to EMIs"*, *"I can only buy things through EMI"*. The app had to make unnecessary expenses visible and help people plan **savings, investment and insurance from their salary**, so they can buy what they need **without borrowing**.
goals: Make unnecessary expenses visible, day by day
Help users put part of every salary aside, including for retirement
Plan ahead for big festival-season spending
Set budgets and goals instead of paying through EMIs
Let users download their daily, monthly and yearly expenses

process.title: User research
process.text: I interviewed potential users with a set of questions about saving, retirement and festival spending, keeping their identity anonymous, and studied behaviour through observation, task analysis and Play Store reviews. The users were 20 to 25, living in Dubai and Chennai, working as junior engineers and developers.

process.title: Competitor analysis
process.text: I compared Wizely, Monefy, Wallet and Mvelopes on mobile app, customer support, offers, price, investment options and ease of use. Only one offered investment, and only one was rated user friendly: the gap RESPAY aims at.

process.title: Persona: Vishnu
process.text: Vishnu, 23, an electrical service engineer working in Dubai, wants to cut unwanted spending, save 25% of his salary and start a retirement plan. His frustrations: no savings, festival-time costs and high bike maintenance.

process.title: Empathy map and user journey
process.text: An empathy map (says, thinks, does, feels) and a user journey map showed where saving breaks down and which moments the app should support.

process.title: Ideation workshop
process.text: In a workshop with fellow designers I turned the users' goals and frustrations into user stories, then compared two designers' solutions for each need: retirement saving, saving part of the salary, festival spending and downloadable expense reports.

process.title: Information architecture and user flow
process.text: Five main areas: Transactions, Budget & goal, Payment, Profile and More. The user flow runs from splash and onboarding through login to each area.

process.title: Design system
process.text: Poppins for all type, a deep blue brand colour with a set of category colours, plus documented iconography, navigation bars and buttons.

process.title: Wireframes
process.text: Paper low-fidelity sketches first, then mid-fidelity frames in grey to settle the layout before the 90+ high-fidelity screens.

features.label: Home
features.title: Every transaction, sliced your way
features.text: After login you land on Transactions: income, expenses and total at the top, then every entry by date and amount, switchable between Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Total and Calendar views. Pay sits in the middle of the tab bar.

features.label: Budget & goal
features.title: Save first, instead of paying EMIs
features.text: The second main page: create a budget to set spending limits, and a goal to save towards with an overview of progress. A simple way to save rather than pay in instalments.

features.label: Status
features.title: See your spending, compared
features.text: Statement data as charts: monthly balance, and spending compared month by month, so users can see their spend and how it changes.

features.label: Accounts
features.title: Your records at a glance
features.text: Available cash and used margin, plus an overview of the last records, with quick buttons to view records or add a new one.

features.label: Bank account
features.title: Add an account safely
features.text: A step-by-step flow to securely enter and submit bank account details.

deliverables: User research: interviews, pain points and demographics
Persona, empathy map and user journey
Design system: type, colour, icons, navigation, buttons
caseStudy.outcome: 90+ screens and a prototype in 14 weeks, from research to high-fidelity UI.

projects.alt: Milton e-commerce website design: home page with product category icons, search, a “Keep It Hot” campaign hero, the Fame Thermosteel bottle offer and sub-brand logos
projects.name: Milton

caseStudy.title: Redesigning Milton's online store
caseStudy.role: UI/UX design: wireframe, layout grid and high-fidelity UI
caseStudy.background: **Milton** sells bottles, flasks, lunch boxes, cookware, storage and kitchen appliances, alongside its sister brands **Treo, Spotzero and Milton ProCook**. This is a *self-initiated redesign* of its online store: I designed the home page and a product page, from a low-fidelity wireframe to high-fidelity UI.
caseStudy.challenge: A catalogue this wide is hard to shop. Someone looking for a lunch box has to get past bottles, cookware and appliances, and offers get lost in the noise. The challenge I set myself: put every category **one tap from the home page**, let shoppers see the **price, the saving and the next step** on every card, and keep Milton's bold red brand.
goals: Every product category one tap away from the home page
Price, MRP and saving readable at a glance on every card
New launches, deals and best sellers easy to tell apart
A product page that answers colour, size and delivery before checkout
Keep Milton's confident red brand look

stats.label: page types designed: home and product

process.title: Low-fidelity wireframe
process.text: I blocked out the home page first: search and account links on top, a row of category tiles, then the campaign hero next to a featured product. The angled section dividers that run through the final design were already part of this stage.

process.title: Layout grid
process.text: Every section sits on one column grid, so category tiles, product cards and banners line up from the header down to the footer.

process.title: High-fidelity UI
process.text: Real products, prices and Milton's red turned the wireframe into a long, shoppable home page: campaign, new launches, deals and category shelves, then reviews and a full footer.

features.label: Navigation
features.title: Every category, one tap away
features.text: A row of 13 line-icon category tiles, from Hot & Cold Bottles and Office Lunch Boxes to Cleaning Products, plus All Products, right under the search bar. Login, Cart and Wishlist stay in the top corner.

features.label: Campaign hero
features.title: The story and the offer, side by side
features.text: “Keep It Hot: keep your drink hot or cold for hours” sits next to a featured product, the Fame Thermosteel Bottle at ₹1,082 with the ₹1,280 MRP struck through, so the hero sells as well as it tells.

features.label: Product cards
features.title: Price and saving first
features.text: Each card leads with the selling price in red, the MRP struck through and a yellow “% off” badge, plus the size and a “New Launch” tag where it helps.

features.label: Shelves
features.title: A long catalogue in small groups
features.text: Top Deals, Trending Bottles, Top Selling Lunchboxes, Cookware and Electrical shelves, broken up by bold category banners, so the page reads as small, scannable groups instead of one endless grid.

features.label: Product page
features.title: Answers before checkout
features.text: Colour swatches, size chips from 350 ml to 1000 ml, quantity, Add to Cart and Shop Now, plus a PIN-code check that shows the expected delivery day.

features.label: Trust
features.title: Reasons to buy
features.text: A short “Why choose us” list and reviews from verified buyers, with star ratings, close the page before the footer.

caseStudy.outcome: A self-initiated redesign: all 13 product categories one tap away, with prices and savings shown first.

projects.description: A self-initiated redesign of Milton's online store: every category one tap away, prices and savings up front, and a product page that answers colour, size and delivery before checkout.

services.name: Product design
services.subtitle: From problem to shipped feature
services.summary: Shaping a product from the problem up — understanding users, mapping flows and turning ideas into something that ships.
services.detail: From user research and interviews to journey maps, user flows, wireframes and clickable prototypes — I turn a fuzzy problem into a clear, tested product direction that designers, developers and stakeholders can build on with confidence.
services.description: Understanding users, mapping flows and turning ideas into something that ships.

services.name: UI/UX design
services.subtitle: Web · Mobile · Design systems
services.summary: Clean, accessible interfaces for web and mobile, built on reusable components so the product stays consistent as it grows.
services.detail: Pixel-accurate web and mobile interfaces built on a reusable component library and design system — responsive layouts, accessible colour and type, every interaction state covered, and a clean, organised Figma handoff for developers.
services.description: Clean, accessible interfaces built on reusable components so the product stays consistent as it grows.

services.name: Graphic design
services.subtitle: Logos · Posters · Brochures
services.summary: Logos, posters and brochures that make a brand instantly recognisable — like the Nexura identity.
services.detail: Brand marks and identity systems, eye-catching posters, and brochures and company decks that present a business clearly — the same colour, typography and layout across every piece, so the brand looks consistent everywhere, like the Nexura identity.
services.description: Logos, posters and brochures that make a brand instantly recognisable — like the Nexura identity.

services.name: Motion design
services.subtitle: UI · Logos · Social
services.summary: Animation that gives products and brands personality, from small UI details to animated logos.
services.detail: Motion that explains and delights — micro-interactions and UI transitions, animated logos and short social pieces made in After Effects, with timing and easing tuned so every movement feels natural and on-brand.
services.description: Animation that gives products and brands personality, from micro-interactions to animated logos.

services.name: Video editing

services.summary: Thumbnails that get clicked, reels that stop the scroll and podcast edits that keep people watching.
